messages:
maria_infra: Heads-up: I'm planning a staged validation for the new NVIDIA driver + firmware + kernel combo to address the spike in Xid errors we've seen on p4/p40 nodes. Goal is to reduce Xid frequency and eliminate the ECC panic we've been hitting on ~3% of the fleet.

maria_infra: TL;DR canary plan: pick 6 nodes across two AZs (low traffic), apply driver 525.60 -> 535.XX, GPU firmware 53->55, kernel 6.1.70 -> 6.1.90 on a snapshot image, run stress + memtest, collect ECC/Xid counters + dmesg for 48h, then evaluate. Rollout only if no regression.

jonas_sre: +1 on canary. When do you want the window? we should pick a low-traffic overnight slot and notify docket oncall. Also want automated rollback hooks. :thumbsup:

maria_infra: @jonas_sre target start 2025-10-17 02:00 UTC (two hour maintenance window). We'll keep auto-rollout off; manual promotion after validation. Rollback plan: reimage to prior snapshot if kernel/driver crash counts exceed baseline.

alex_ml: Have we correlated model-serving pod restarts to Xids? Last week we saw two model restarts tied to GPU resets. If you push firmware, can you validate that CUDA context loss count stays at 0?

maria_infra: Good point. We'll capture metrics: nvidia_smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,driver_version,gpu_busy --format=csv and node_exporter GPU exporter (gpu_reset_count, ecc_uncorrectable_count, xid_errors). We'll also run a short inference shard against a canary model to see OOM/context loss.

maria_infra: Initial pre-upgrade snapshot of one candidate node: 
```
# nvidia-smi -q | egrep "Driver Version|Product Name|Ecc Errors|Xid"
Driver Version : 525.60.13
Product Name : NVIDIA Tesla T4
Ecc Errors (Volatile) : 12
Ecc Errors (Aggregate) : 0
Xid Errors : 24
```

maria_infra: Example dmesg snippet we've been seeing: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:0000001e) 58f0b8 00000000 00000000 00000000
[ 12345.678902] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679000] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: GPU fault: 13 0x50e0
```

tanya_eng: For the kernel bump, please include the exact kernelconfig we used last time. We need CONFIG_IOMMU and PCIe ACS options recorded in case of regressions. Also ensure kexec-based fallback is disabled on those canaries so we can fully re-image.

maria_infra: Will do. Validation checklist: 
- [ ] Snapshot baseline metrics over 24h
- [ ] Upgrade driver + firmware + kernel on canary image
- [ ] Run stressapptest (8 workers) for 3h + memtest for 1h
- [ ] Run 1000 sample inference requests (latency percentile)
- [ ] Monitor prometheus alerts for gpu_reset_count > baseline + 2sd and xid_errors > 0
- [ ] Upload logs to s3 path s3://redwood-ops/gpu-fw-validation/1750301234/

jonas_sre: Add: enable auditd to capture any kcred/kernel-oops messages and trigger an incident if GPU resets > 1 in 1h. I'll add a temporary alert rule.

opsbot: deploy-bot: starting maintenance window for nodes: canary-1, canary-2, canary-3, canary-4, canary-5, canary-6 at 2025-10-17T02:00:00Z

maria_infra: Small gotcha: we've seen Xid 79 tend to appear when certain NVidia firmware+kernel combos interact poorly under sustained small-batch inference. We'll include a specific test: 75% 1-token requests at QPS 200 for 30min to try to reproduce.

alex_ml: If we see regressions, should we try different driver-only or firmware-only permutations before rolling back entire kernel? Could save time if one component is culprit.

maria_infra: Agreed. Plan B: if canary fails, iterate binary search: try driver-only on same kernel; if still failing, driver+firmware; if still failing, kernel rollback. We'll log which permutation produced the first failure.

tanya_eng: One more: ensure we capture PCIe AER logs and run `setpci` to query link status after firmware apply. Past flaky cards showed link drops.

maria_infra: Noted. I'll add `lspci -vvv` and `dmesg | grep -i aer` to the collector.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary-1 upgrade: driver update applied, firmware flashed, kernel installed, node reboot queued

maria_infra: After first canary cycle (6h in), summary: 
- canary-1: 0 new Xid, 0 gpu resets, passes stress tests
- canary-2: 1 Xid (Xid 31) within first hour, triggered a single GPU reset, container restarted, no crashdump; investigating
- canary-3..6: no new Xids

maria_infra: Logs for canary-2 show repeated ECC volatile increments prior to Xid: 
```
Ecc Errors (Volatile) : 45 -> 48
[ 45678.123456] NVRM: Xid (0004:0000001f) 1234abcd ...
```

jonas_sre: Hmm canary-2 might have a marginal card. Is it in same batch as some previously replaced nodes? Check serial. If it's hardware, we should mark for drain+replace rather than blaming firmware.

maria_infra: Good catch. Serial SN-1221 flagged. Historically had slightly higher ECC counts. I'll mark for replacement and exclude from rollout decisions.

alex_ml: So excluding canary-2, the rest look good. Any perf delta on p50/p95?

maria_infra: Perf: p50 +2% latency, p95 +4% in synthetic inference test (within expected variance). No increased memory errors on non-excluded nodes.

jonas_sre: Given results, I'm comfortable proceeding to a small 10-node pilot next week, but require safeguards: auto-rollback script, oncall pairing, and drain-replace flagging for any node with ecc_uncorrectable > 0.

maria_infra: I'll prepare runbook and the rollback script (uses fleetctl to reimage and tag node). I'll post the runbook link in #incidents and ping oncall 30m before start.

deploy-bot: runbook uploaded: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-fw-validation-1750301234

maria_infra: Thanks all. If anyone wants to be on the pilot warroom, ping me. Will post final pilot schedule tomorrow. :rocket:
